categories.main_business_segments: TOKYOTOKEIBA CO., LTD. operates four main business segments: Public Racing Business (leasing and management of horse racing and auto race facilities), Amusement Park Business (operation of Tokyo Summerland), Warehouse Leasing Business (leasing of logistics facilities), and Service Business (management and leasing of commercial facilities, office buildings, and air conditioning equipment services).
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s core operations rely on facility management, large-scale event operations, digital ticketing and remote betting systems (notably the SPAT4 online betting platform), and sustainable facility maintenance. In the amusement park segment, energy-efficient infrastructure, renewable energy (solar and biomass), and advanced environmental management practices are emphasized.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include local governments (notably the Special Ward Horse Racing Association), racing fans (both on-site and online), amusement park visitors, logistics companies (for warehouse leasing), and tenants of commercial and office properties. The company also serves the broader leisure and entertainment market in the Tokyo metropolitan area.
categories.geographic_coverage: Operations are concentrated in the Tokyo metropolitan area and surrounding regions, with major facilities in Tokyo (Ota, Shinagawa, Akiruno), Chiba, Gunma, and other select locations in Niigata, Ibaraki, and Miyagi. All business activities are domestic, with no overseas operations.
categories.supply_chain_position: The company operates primarily downstream, providing end-user services such as facility leasing, event hosting, entertainment, and property management. In warehouse leasing, it acts as a landlord to logistics operators, while in public racing and amusement parks, it is the direct service provider to consumers and local governments.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include digital transformation (DX), ESG initiatives, and sustainability (notably CO2 reduction and renewable energy adoption). The company is focused on enhancing customer experience through digital platforms, improving operational efficiency, and investing in facility upgrades. There is no significant proprietary R&D, but ongoing investment in IT systems, environmental technologies, and facility modernization is emphasized.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated primarily through facility leasing (to local governments for racing, to tenants for warehouses and commercial properties), direct sales (amusement park admissions and services), and service fees (air conditioning and facility management). A significant portion of public racing revenue is linked to a percentage of betting ticket sales.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: TOKYOTOKEIBA is a leading player in the niche market of public racing facility leasing and regional amusement parks in the Tokyo area. Its main competitors are other regional racing facility operators, amusement park companies, and logistics facility landlords. The company holds a strong, stable position due to its long-term contracts with local governments and unique asset base.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending December 2024, consolidated sales reached approximately 40.4 billion yen, with operating profit of 13.9 billion yen and net profit attributable to shareholders of 9.7 billion yen. The company has shown steady growth in revenue and profit over the past five years, maintains a high equity ratio (over 70%), and continues to expand its asset base through new facility investments.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: TOKYOTOKEIBA differentiates itself through its unique combination of public racing, leisure, and logistics facility businesses, strong relationships with local governments, and a focus on safe, sustainable, and customer-friendly spaces. Its digital betting platform (SPAT4) and commitment to ESG and community engagement further enhance its value proposition.
